verdict.headline: The weakest private hiring since January barely dented the odds of a Fed rate hike
verdict.label: ADP printed 38,000 private jobs against a ~47,000 consensus and September hike odds fell only to ~64% from 68.2%. Gold settled -2.86% at $4,325 and silver -3.73% at $64.13. The 10-year touched 4.81%, highest since November 2023, then closed back at 4.79%, unchanged. S&P 500 +0.46% to 7,666.60, Dow +0.56%, Nasdaq +0.45%, Russell 2000 +1.12%. Broadcom fell 5% after hours on a $34.8B Q4 guide against $35.03B expected.
verdict.rationale_short: A labour miss bought no dovish repricing because the inflation input is not coming from the labour market: the Beige Book, published the same afternoon, reported input prices rising strongly under tariffs and energy while selling-price increases stayed moderate. Equities rose because the long end declined to make a new high, not because the policy path eased — the Russell 2000 led at +1.12% after being Tuesday's worst at -1.23%, the signature of a pause in a rate move rather than a reversal. Gold's fourth consecutive decline through an active US-Iran escalation says the Gulf is still being priced as an inflation input rather than a fear event. Friday's payrolls is what actually resolves the hike trade: a print near the 50-55K consensus with earnings at or under 0.3% breaks it, above 150,000 with hot earnings extends it.

supporting_data.label: ADP private payrolls rose 38,000 in August against a ~47,000 consensus and July's upwardly revised 46,000 — the slowest month since January; manufacturing shed 17,000 and professional and business services 16,000
CME FedWatch odds of a September rate hike fell to roughly 64% from 68.2% a day earlier

Beige Book: activity up modestly and prices up moderately, with input prices rising strongly under tariffs and energy costs; the pace of price increases slowed in three of twelve districts and was unchanged in eight
The 10-year yield touched 4.81%, its highest since November 2023, before easing to 4.79% and pausing a five-session rally
Gold settled at $4,325 (-2.86%) and silver at $64.13 (-3.73%) on higher real yields and a firm dollar, despite the Iran escalation
Broadcom fell 5% after hours: Q3 revenue $29.59B beat $29.36B and EPS $3.32 beat $3.24, with AI semi revenue $16.7B up 221%, but Q4 revenue guidance of $34.8B missed the $35.03B consensus

watchlist_mentions.note: Gold settled at $4,325, down 2.86%, a fourth consecutive decline through an active US-Iran escalation, with silver down 3.73% to $64.13. The tape is still pricing the Gulf as an inflation input rather than a fear event; a move back above $4,450 alongside a firmer barrel would mark that changing.
Rose about 3.3%, the best performer in the Dow and the largest single contributor to its 295-point gain, on no company news — the same duration trade that sold it Tuesday, running the other way.

WTI settled at $90.72 (+0.56%) with Brent at $94.86 (+0.23%), a fourth session above $94. Transit volumes through Hormuz, not strike counts, remain the marker that would convert the premium into a measured supply disruption.

Held near $77,000 and shrugged off the ADP miss, keeping the $76,661 support above the price for a second session. Crypto trades the Labor Day weekend's Hormuz headlines with no cash equity market to absorb them until September 8.

Added 0.46% to 7,666.60, reclaiming the 7,650 level lost Tuesday and snapping a three-day slide. The gain came from the long end declining to make a new high rather than from an easier policy path, which is why the rate-sensitive Russell led at +1.12%.

trade_setups.thesis: ADP's 38,000 sits against a consensus near 50,000-55,000 for the BLS print, with unemployment forecast at 4.1% and average hourly earnings at 3.0% year over year. The two series have diverged sharply this year — July payrolls fell 23,000 against an +83,000 consensus — and the hike trade barely moved on ADP, which means the BLS number is carrying the whole resolution.
trade_setups.entry: A print near consensus with average hourly earnings at or under 0.3% is what breaks the hike trade; above 150,000 with hot earnings extends it
trade_setups.invalidation: A revision-heavy report that muddies both series leaves the 64% odds intact into the September 15-16 FOMC

trade_setups.thesis: The long bond has traded through 5.30% twice and settled under it every time, closing near 5.26% today in a fourth session inside the level. Treasury's enlarged long-dated buyback operations begin September 9 at $4 billion-plus per operation, so the structural bid arrives after Friday's payrolls rather than before it.
trade_setups.entry: A daily close above 5.30% marks the level crossed rather than tagged; a close under 5.15% says the buyback bid is being anticipated
trade_setups.invalidation: A payrolls print that pulls hike odds under 50% removes the policy input driving the long end
trade_setups.horizon: Through September 9, when the buyback operations begin

trade_setups.thesis: Gold has fallen for four consecutive sessions through a week of US strikes on Iranian targets, settling 2.86% lower at $4,325 with silver down 3.73%. The market is treating the Gulf as a source of inflation rather than of fear, which is the assumption underneath every other position on the page.
trade_setups.entry: A move back above $4,450 alongside a firmer barrel says a haven premium is being paid and the regime has changed; continued declines with Brent above $94 confirm the inflation framing
trade_setups.invalidation: A Brent close back under $90 removes the inflation impulse and the framing question with it
trade_setups.horizon: Days, resolving around Friday's payrolls and the Labor Day weekend

bear_case: The read treats a four-point move in hike odds as evidence the labour market no longer matters to the Fed, when the simpler explanation is that one private survey rarely moves a committee eleven days out. ADP has diverged from the BLS all year, and the Beige Book's own data was collected on or before August 24 — before the oil move it is being used to explain. Gold's decline is as easily read as position unwinding into a long weekend as a statement about the inflation regime. If Friday's payrolls prints near consensus with earnings at or under 0.3% and hike odds fall under 50%, this read no longer holds.
